events.title: French protectorate
hints: A queen signed a protection treaty with a naval officer in April 1887.
Two small island groups were ruled from afar by a Resident.
A referendum in 1959 led to overseas-territory status in 1961.
events.summary: In April 1887 the queen of Uvea signed a treaty with France establishing a protectorate, and the chiefs of Futuna followed in 1888. After a 1959 referendum, the islands became a French overseas territory in 1961.

events.title: US military base
hints: Marines landed in May 1942, soon after a Vichy government was overthrown.
Thousands of troops built an airfield and camps.
The garrison was about as large as the local population.
events.summary: After a Free French ship deposed the Vichy-aligned administration, US Marines landed in May 1942. They built an airfield and camps on the island, with thousands of troops stationed there, roughly equal to the local population, until the war ended.

events.title: Tongan invasions
hints: Warriors from a maritime empire built a stone fortress on the larger of the two islands in the 15th century.
The invasions of the 15th and 16th centuries met varying levels of resistance.
The smaller island kept more of its older culture, while the larger one changed its society, language and culture more deeply.
events.summary: During the 15th and 16th centuries Tongan forces invaded the islands of Wallis (Uvea) and Futuna, building the Talietumu fortress on Wallis, and met varying levels of resistance. The islands accepted different degrees of assimilation: Futuna kept more of its pre-Tongan culture, while Wallis underwent greater changes in its society, language and culture.
